review_notes: I read the whole file from the supplied text and did not open any related sources. The only repetition is in the pentagon and triangle proofs. Both use the same induction pattern on `bimoduleTensor_induction_on`, with the same additive `ha` branch: `simp only [bimoduleTensorTmul_add_left, map_add, ...]`. The pentagon proof uses that branch twice. This is a one-line `simp` closing a routine additivity step, and the rubric says moving duplicated branches into a helper is insufficient. The pure-tensor cases differ: the pentagon is closed by unfolding `tmul` lemmas, and the triangle needs `bimoduleTensorTmul_balance`. No shared lemma would hold nontrivial reasoning. The two unitor-naturality blocks in `bimoduleMonoidalCategory` are mirror-image three-line rewrites (`have h := ...; simp only [← ...] at h; exact h`). They are short routine unfolding, and a helper would not improve readability. The `Components` simp lemmas are all `rfl` and are separate API statements, not repeated proofs. I am fairly confident there is no justified finding under this rubric.
